clue.text: It shows us how to prepare food ready to eat without notes

definitions.text: It shows us how to prepare food

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for ready to eat sits around the notes

parts.note: fruit that is ready to eat is ripe
E and C are both musical notes

explanation.surface: A description of something you can eat straight away, needing no cooking or written instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here means outside, not lacking: RIPE wraps around E and C, two notes of the scale.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of cooking instructions tells the cook how a dish is made.

clue.text: Tease a student with monotonous bawdiness

parts.note: to rib is to tease
L is the learner plate letter, a student driver
dry means dull or monotonous

explanation.surface: Mocking a boring pupil for crude humour.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribaldry is coarse, vulgar humour.

clue.text: Humorous member put out by new shape of road markers

indicators.note: put out by means one letter is evicted and another takes its place

parts.note: comical means humorous
M is short for member, as in Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A funny club member ejected by a newcomer, all about traffic cones.
explanation.walkthrough: Road markers are traffic cones; 'put out by' swaps M for N.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic cones taper to a point, so their form is cone-like.

clue.text: He claims entitlement to parking in the case of a pram!

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
re means regarding or in the case of
a pram is also a small flat-bottomed boat, a tender carrying goods to a ship

explanation.surface: A parent asserts a right to a parking spot because of a baby carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pram' looks like a baby carriage but is a ship's small boat, a tender.
explanation.definitionFit: A claimant to a throne, such as the Old Pretender, asserts a right to it.

clue.text: Thus the Italian man describes the Vespers of 1282

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quotation as printed
il is the Italian word for the
Ian is a man's name

explanation.surface: Someone notes that an Italian man gives an account of a medieval church service.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sicilian Vespers was the 1282 uprising in Palermo against French rule, so the word describing those Vespers is the adjective for the island.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1282 revolt against the Angevin French began in Palermo and is known by the island's adjective.

clue.text: Empathy recognised in the papers

definitions.meaning: the feeling of sharing another person's experience
the papers that prove who you are, or recognition of someone as reported

explanation.surface: A newspaper reports that compassion has been acknowledged.
explanation.definitionFit: Identifying with someone is feeling empathy; papers proving who you are are ID documents.

clue.text: State of some who had it withdrawn in retirement

indicators.note: withdrawn in retirement means the run of letters retreats, read backwards
some means only part of the words is taken

explanation.surface: The condition of a few people who had something taken away when they stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: OHADI sits inside 'who had it'; 'withdrawn in retirement' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the fifty US states, in the north-west.

clue.text: Nightmare for copper kept below in capsized vessel

indicators.note: kept below means in this down clue the metal sits under the little word in

parts.note: taken as written
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: capsized means the boat is turned upside down, read upwards in a down clue

parts.note: a sub is a submarine, a vessel

explanation.surface: A bad dream about a policeman held beneath decks in an overturned ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is CU; SUB capsized gives BUS.
explanation.definitionFit: An incubus is an oppressive evil spirit, hence a nightmare.

clue.text: Loony found treasure up a tree

parts.note: a nut is a crazy person, a loony

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a gem is a treasure

explanation.surface: A madman discovered riches up in the branches.
explanation.definitionFit: The East Indian evergreen whose seed gives the spice.

clue.text: Blue fluffy substance surrounded by heaps of rubbish?

parts.note: down is fine soft fluff or feathers
being amid tips or refuse heaps is being in the dumps

explanation.surface: Blue fluff lying amid piles of refuse.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'in the dumps' is taken literally here.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue means feeling depressed or low-spirited.

clue.text: Function of troop carrying eastern flag

indicators.note: carrying means the combined words hold a letter between them

parts.note: a band is a troop or company of people
a role is a function or job

explanation.surface: Describing what a body of soldiers does in bearing a flag from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Function of troop' means the troop's function, so the function word comes second; 'carrying' has the pair hold the eastern letter between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A banderole is a long narrow streamer or pennant flown from a mast or lance.

clue.text: Cravat for a countryman like James Hogg

parts.note: James Hogg, the Ettrick Shepherd, was a Scottish poet, so a fellow countryman of his is a Scot

explanation.surface: A neckpiece chosen for a rural poet from the Borders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Countryman' suggests a rustic, but it means a fellow national: James Hogg was a Scottish writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide neck scarf worn tucked in at the collar, named after the racecourse where it was fashionable.

clue.text: Stand for books in Design Centre on the left

indicators.note: on here means the left-hand letter is placed at the start, ahead of the rearranged word

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left

indicators.note: the letters of centre are put into a new design, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A bookstand displayed at a design centre, positioned on the left-hand side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the left' places L at the front of ECTERN, the rearrangement of CENTRE that 'in Design' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A reading desk with a sloping top, used to hold a book for someone reading aloud in church or a hall.

clue.text: He's left the money in Vladivostok? Bother

indicators.note: left means departed, so those letters go out of the word the

parts.note: taken as written before letters go
the pronoun he, as letters
Vladivostok is in Russia, whose currency is the rouble

explanation.surface: Someone has departed leaving cash in a Russian port city, which causes difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He's left the' reads as 'he has left the': take HE out of THE to leave T.
explanation.definitionFit: Trouble and bother both mean difficulty or inconvenience.

clue.text: Angry that the state took precedence

parts.note: RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state
led means went first or took precedence

explanation.surface: Someone was annoyed because the government was given priority.
explanation.definitionFit: Riled means irritated or annoyed, a form of being cross.

clue.text: The sharpest condition in book about bonds

indicators.note: about means the book abbreviation goes around the other pieces

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a book of the Bible
if introduces a condition
ties are bonds or links

explanation.surface: The best-tuned condition is found in a book on financial bonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bonds' suggests finance, and 'condition' a state of health; 'about' puts the book around the other two.
explanation.definitionFit: Niftiest means smartest or cleverest, the superlative of a slangy word for neat and sharp.

clue.text: Legal rights in leisure activities

definitions.meaning: shares or stakes in property that the law recognises

explanation.surface: A list of legal entitlements tucked among someone's hobbies.
explanation.definitionFit: A stake in property is a legal right; hobbies are what one pursues in spare time.

clue.text: Said to look smaller but unlined

indicators.note: said means the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: to look smaller is to seem less

explanation.surface: Reportedly it appears more compact but has no lining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unlined' means without join lines, as in seamless stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no joins or visible stitching is smooth and without lines.

clue.text: A Papist in China, perhaps very confused

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the country name
perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged another way

parts.note: RC stands for Roman Catholic, a papist

explanation.surface: A Catholic in China may be very bewildered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Papist' is an old, hostile word for a Roman Catholic; 'in' puts it inside the country before 'perhaps' rearranges the lot, making NARCHIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something anarchic is chaotic and lawless, in total disorder.

clue.text: Informal wear of fellow briefly nursing injured leg

indicators.note: nursing means holding the other piece inside
briefly means the name loses its tail

parts.note: Nigel is a man's name, a fellow

indicators.note: injured means the letters of leg are damaged and reshaped

explanation.surface: A man in a loose robe tends a hurt leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow' is a stock man's name cut short by 'briefly'; 'injured' rearranges the leg, which 'nursing' holds after the name's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A negligee is a loose light robe or dressing gown worn at home.

clue.text: Burden for leaders of team crossing border

indicators.note: crossing means the leading letters straddle another piece
the leaders of a word are its opening letters

parts.note: a hem is the border of a garment

explanation.surface: A heavy load for the captains of a side as they cross a frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: Burden here is the refrain or main topic of a song or speech, not a heavy load.
explanation.definitionFit: The burden of a song or argument is its central subject or refrain.

clue.text: Part of record is lyric poem

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A section of a disc contains a song-like poem.
explanation.definitionFit: An episode is one instalment or section of a series or story.

clue.text: Sergeant-major involved in climbing a mountain? It's in the blood

indicators.note: involved in means one piece is wrapped inside another
climbing in a down clue means the letters are read upward

parts.note: an alp is a mountain

explanation.surface: An army sergeant-major taking part in a mountain ascent: it's in his blood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbing' turns A ALP to PLAA, which SM enters.
explanation.definitionFit: Plasma is the pale fluid carrying the blood cells.

clue.text: Convict with drawback — he falls behind

parts.note: a lag is an old slang word for a convict
draw is drag, read back

explanation.surface: A prisoner with a disadvantage lags at the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawback' is draw back: DRAG turned round gives GARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A laggard is a straggler or slowcoach who trails the rest.

clue.text: Letter disclosing a restless desire

parts.note: an itch is a restless craving

explanation.surface: A note that reveals an uneasy craving.
explanation.definitionFit: Aitch is the spelt-out name of the eighth letter of the alphabet.

clue.text: But some may not think it's supporting the right party!

definitions.text: But some may not think it's supporting the right party!

parts.words: But some may not think it's supporting the right party!
parts.note: the clue describes the creed of those backing the Conservatives, which opponents would say is the wrong party to back

explanation.surface: A political jibe: some doubt that backing this side is correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Toryism is the political philosophy of supporting the British Conservative Party, the party of the right.

clue.text: Grudgingly provide for a sandpiper

definitions.meaning: a small wading bird of the sandpiper family

explanation.surface: Someone grudgingly hands out food for a shore bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To give in meagre amounts is to skimp; the wading bird is a small sandpiper relative of the dunlin.

clue.text: Monet soon produced a gem

indicators.note: produced means the letters of the painter's name and soon are made into something new

explanation.surface: The Impressionist painter will shortly create a fine piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Produced' signals rearranging MONET SOON.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearly feldspar prized as a semi-precious stone.

clue.text: Heartbroken American found a nymph in spring

indicators.note: broken means the letters of heart are smashed apart and reset

parts.note: USA abbreviates the United States of America

explanation.surface: A heartbroken American finds a woodland spirit in the springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' is a water source, not the season: in Greek myth the nymph was turned into a fountain in Sicily.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth she fled the river god Alpheus and was changed into a fountain at Syracuse.

clue.text: Estimate taxes finally imposed on foolish people

parts.note: asses are foolish people

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of taxes

explanation.surface: Working out how taxes in the end are laid upon idiots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Imposed on' puts the S after ASSES.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaluate or gauge a value or amount.
